maya: Heads-up — we've been seeing intermittent 20–40% tail latency spikes on the Ampere pool since last night. Pattern looks like a kernel-selection flip around ~1k tokens, sometimes correlated with a KV cache miss/evict. Can someone post a compact nsys 'playbook' I can run quickly to capture the kernel switch without collecting a 5GB trace?

liam: Short answer: NVTX brackets + short capture windows + filter to cuda+osrt+nVTX. Keep sample rate low and prefer event tracing (osrt) over heavy sampling. Example I use:

liam: ```
# pid is the serving worker pid (get via ps or pgrep)
nsys profile --output=trace_kernflip --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \
  --capture-range=process:%PID% \
  --duration=12s \
  --sample=cpu:200 \
  --stop-on-range-exit

# then convert: nsys stats trace_kernflip.qdrep --report=timeline
```

liam: Two tips: 1) put NVTX around the code that switches batching heuristics / KV evict, 2) run multiple short capture attempts (10–15s) rather than one long run. :thumbsup:

sophia: For the NVTX approach I usually do explicit markers in runtime:

sophia: ```cpp
NVTX_PUSH_RANGE("KERNEL_SWITCH_START");
// call that codepath: recompute kernel selection, maybe call quantized kernel
NVTX_POP_RANGE();

NVTX_PUSH_RANGE("KERNEL_SWITCH_END");
NVTX_POP_RANGE();
```

sophia: Then nsys can do `--capture-range=nvtx:KERNEL_SWITCH_START:KERNEL_SWITCH_END` so you only capture those moments. Saves a lot of file size. Also combine with `--sample=none` if you only need the event timeline — sampling bloats output.

chen: Quick caution about sampling bias — if you use very short durations you can miss rare kernel hotpaths. Two pragmatic runs:
1) NVTX bracket capture focused on the suspected codepath (tiny window).
2) One longer low-frequency sample (e.g., --sample=cpu:50, 60s) to catch any scheduler jitter or host-side stalls.

chen: If you suspect KV-cache invalidation triggers the flip, add NVTX marks around cache set/evict and around the prefix-serving call. Then grep the timeline for cuda kernel names changing right after the evict marker.

maya: Nice. Any easy grep/incantation to find kernel handoffs in the qdrep? I don't want to open the big GUI each time.

liam: You can use `nsys stats`/`nsys export` to a `sqlite`/CSV then grep. Minimal command:

liam: ```bash
nsys stats trace_kernflip.qdrep --report=timeline --format=csv --output=trace_kernflip.timeline.csv
# then: grep -n "kernel_name" trace_kernflip.timeline.csv | sed -n '1,200p'
```

liam: Or just filter by NVTX region column to see which kernels ran inside your bracket.

ops-bot: Reminder: if you upload traces to s3, scrub IPs/keys. Use `tools/trace-scrub` before sharing. Uploaded: s3://redwood-traces/4361209876-maya (placeholder).

sophia: One more micro-tip: on Ampere we saw kernel selection flip when seq_len crossed the model's block boundary due to a different matmul kernel being chosen. Add a synthetic run with token lengths around the boundary (e.g., 900, 1000, 1100) so you can reliably reproduce the flip during capture runs.

maya: Perfect — I'll add NVTX around cache evict + kernel decision, run several 12s captures with the short command, and post the qdrep. Thanks all! :rocket:
